transcript.text: dyson keeps pulsin on n off like its stutterin, wont stay on proper. batt is full. pls help

Pulsing on and off usually means the vacuum is protecting itself due to restricted airflow. Please switch it off and unplug it, or remove the battery first. Then empty the bin and wash the filters in cold water. It is vital that a washed filter is completely dry for at least 24 hours before putting it back in, as even slight dampness causes pulsing. The app shows a picture to help you with this process. Was a filter clogged or damp (and is it sorted), is a filter damaged, or were they clean and dry already?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
its a v8 animal. emptied the bin, was full of dog hair, still pulsin. never washed the filter, didnt know u could. its grey not purple lol. no burning smell or heat btw

Thanks for confirming your Dyson V8 details and that the filters have been sorted. Please try using the vacuum again once you are sure the filters are fully dry. This simple step often resolves performance issues related to moisture in the filtration system. Is it running steadily now, or still pulsing / cutting out?
i only emptied the bin, filter not washed yet. still pulsin. how do i wash it

Thanks for letting us know the pulsing continues even after sorting the filters. Please switch off and unplug the vacuum (or remove the battery) before starting. Detach the wand and floorhead, then look through each part to check for blockages. Also inspect the bin inlet; a coin dropped through the wand should fall straight out. Did you find a blockage and clear it, is there one you can't shift, is a hose split, or was it all clear?

Thanks for letting us know you haven’t retested yet. A jammed brush bar can also cause the pulsing issue. Please switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Then, turn the floorhead over and clear any hair or thread from the brush bar. Check that it turns freely by hand. Was it jammed or tangled (and is it clear now), is it broken, or did it turn freely?
